meta.title: Starship Flight 15 · Contingency · Indian Ocean
about: Contingency profile: Contingency · Indian Ocean. Pre-launch model: Flight 14's zone-fitted orbit with the Flight 15 timeline, a Super Heavy return and a 3-DOF entry to the Pad 2 tower; not telemetry.
Hazard areas are the Flight 14 warnings; Flight 15 warnings were not yet published, so their windows are re-timed model values.
notes: Pre-launch model, not telemetry and not an official ephemeris. Window 22:45-00:00 UTC on 13-14 Nov 2026 (16:45-18:00 CST), from the SpaceX mission page; T0 22:45 is the window open, not an announced liftoff time.

Orbit plane: Flight 14's fit to the September 2026 navigational warnings (i 30.58 deg, 275 km circular with J2 secular rates, node 2.1 deg east of the pad, the ascent steering into the plane). SpaceX: Flight 15 flies the same altitude and inclination. The orbital rate is scaled by +0.0013 (nodal period 89.629 min, as a 269 km mean orbit) so that the modeled catch happens at the official T+22:32:34; Flight 14's deorbit telemetry read 270 km against that model's 275.

Ascent: a shaped kinematic profile (Max Q 11.5 km at T+58 s, MECO 66 km and 1.5 km/s at T+2:19, SECO 150 km and 15 deg downrange at T+8:09, the Flight 14 assumptions) that ends on the suborbital coast ellipse in position and velocity. Insertion at T+26:10 is modeled at the burn start as an instantaneous circularisation at apogee.

Super Heavy: 2-D point mass from the MECO state; 36 s boostback (46 m/s^2, 1655 m/s), ballistic fall with US76 drag (ballistic coefficient 3400 kg/m^2), 25 s landing burn to rest on the Pad 2 tower, arriving from the Gulf. Apogee 102 km, 81 km maximum downrange, 634 m/s at the landing-burn start. Illustrative: the boostback and landing-burn throttles are not public.

Descents: the Starship calibrated on Flight 14's reconstructed entry (3-DOF point mass, rotating WGS-84 Earth, J2, US Standard Atmosphere 1976, modified-Newtonian belly-first aerodynamics with a 55 deg hypersonic angle of attack, L/D 0.70, ballistic coefficient 331 kg/m^2, bank steering that fades out below Mach 1.5, a 10 s one-Raptor deorbit burn). The constant bank is a model choice; SpaceX describes a series of small turns over sparsely populated areas.

Hazard zones are the Flight 14 navigational-warning polygons (NAVAREA IV 922/26, HYDROPAC 2751/26, NAVAREA XII 657/26 = HYDROPAC 2761/26, HYDROPAC 2750/26). SpaceX states the Flight 15 contingency areas are the same precleared areas. No Flight 15 warnings had been published when this was built; the daily windows shown are the Flight 14 windows re-timed to the Flight 15 launch window and the late-Hawaii window comes from the model.

Sunlight: geometric WGS-84 occultation of the Sun centre with JPL DE440s at 60 s cadence. Shifting T0 keeps the Earth-fixed path and moves the Sun. Cities beyond the template list are added for the Americas, the Pacific and the deorbit regions; the sky chart opens on South Padre Island.

Sources: spacex.com/launches/starship-flight-15 and spacex.com/updates (7 Nov 2026) for the timeline, window, catch description and contingency areas; the Flight 14 model at github.com/exoplanet5/Starship-IFT14 for the plane, zones and ship calibration.

No insertion burn: from SECO the ship coasts on the suborbital ellipse (perigee -74 km) with the 26 Starlink V3 still aboard (+50 t assumed, ballistic coefficient 475 kg/m^2) and steers with a 81 deg bank, reversed at T+00:51:30, to the middle of the Indian Ocean zone; 5.2 g maximum.
